prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across the five frames, the bright tree trunk, its low brick planter, the nearby ground, and the left-edge gate are the nearest surfaces, roughly 0.5–2 m from the camera wearer; the two people beyond the low wall appear about 3–5 m away and approximately 1–2 m apart. The house and rear courtyard remain farther away, roughly 6–12 m, with the people standing in front of them and partly overlapping the darker background. As the view shifts right, the tree moves from near center to the left, while the people move from left/center toward center/right; no clear large approach or retreat is visible. The depth map makes foreground–background separation and the tree's occlusion of the courtyard clearer than RGB alone, but its absolute metre scale is uncalibrated and several person, foliage, wall, and ground boundaries contain halos or inconsistent depths.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map consistently isolates two people beyond the planter/wall, usually with one person to the left and slightly behind the other; they are roughly 3–5 m from the camera wearer and about 1–2 m from each other. Their masks shift from the left side in frame 1 toward the right side by frame 5 as the camera viewpoint turns, and neither person appears within the camera wearer's arm's reach. A small potted-plant detection appears high in frame 2, and a bottle detection appears below the people in frame 5, but most scene structures—including the tree, planter, wall, house, blocks, and tools—are not segmented. The masks reveal person silhouettes more clearly than RGB where clothing blends with the shaded courtyard, but they provide little direct depth or facing information and look unreliable around limbs, overlapping boundaries, the tiny plant, and the bottle label.
descriptions.pose: Only one usable body skeleton is detected, in frame 4 on the person to the right of the tree and beyond the low wall, about 3–5 m from the camera wearer; the other person and nearly all bodies in the remaining frames are missed. The detected torso is upright, with the head above it and one lower point beneath, but the sparse joints do not reliably establish exact arm reach, gaze direction, or whether the person faces the camera wearer. Relative to the scene, this skeleton is well beyond the camera wearer's arm's reach and close to the second person, roughly 1–2 m away, while the foreground planter and tree remain between or beside the camera and the people. The pose map can expose body orientation and joint placement when RGB silhouettes are small, but here it is highly incomplete, lacks hand detections, and is too sparse to support reliable turning or approach/retreat estimates across the five frames.
